title: PERC rule
subtitle: PE rule-out in selected very-low-risk adults
summary: PERC is used only after pulmonary embolism has already been judged clinically very unlikely and a credible alternative diagnosis is more likely.
population: Adults with an estimated PE pre-test probability below about 15%.
A credible alternative diagnosis is more likely than PE.
exclusions: Do not apply when PE remains a realistic diagnosis.
Do not use to assess other causes of chest pain or dyspnoea.

criteria.label: PE is already judged clinically very unlikely
criteria.description: Estimated pre-test probability below about 15%, with no unresolved features making PE a realistic diagnosis.

criteria.label: A credible alternative diagnosis is more likely
criteria.description: For example chest-wall pain reproduced by focal palpation or movement, without unexplained dyspnoea, syncope, hypoxia or unilateral leg findings.

criteria.label: Recent surgery or trauma requiring hospitalisation

results.label: PERC not yet applicable
interpretation: Confirm that PE is already clinically very unlikely and that a credible alternative diagnosis is more likely.

results.label: PERC negative
interpretation: Within a correctly selected low-risk population, PE is sufficiently unlikely that further PE testing is generally not required. PE is not impossible, and overall disposition must consider other diagnoses.

results.label: PERC positive
interpretation: PE cannot be ruled out using PERC. This does not diagnose PE; continue through the appropriate PE assessment pathway.

overrides: A normal ECG does not rule out NSTEMI.
Other serious causes of chest pain must be assessed separately.
limitations: Eligibility is a prerequisite and is not part of the numerical score.
All eight PERC criteria must be negative for a negative result.

clinicalValidation.reviewNotes: Formal clinical verification has not yet been recorded. Population, exclusions, thresholds, calculations, wording and implementation tests must be checked against the cited source.
